newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA MAY DEFER PROJECTS, BIG IMPORTS - ANWAR.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA MAY DEFER PROJECTS, BIG IMPORTS - ANWAR.

text.p: Malaysia may defer some big import items and less important infrastructure projects to cushion the impact of a weak ringgit on the trade account, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday.

"There will be an impact if nothing is done," the national news agency Bernama quoted Anwar as telling reporters in the town of Sepang after visiting the site of the country's new international airport.
He said the government would review projects that have not yet started and were not considered "critical" or strategic to Malaysia, Bernama quoted him as saying.
Projects like the Kuala Lumpur International Airport and sea ports were among those considered strategic, but "there are maybe some projects which we think we can defer", Anwar said.

The government was also looking at how to reduce the import bill, which would likely escalate much more than expected due to the weaker ringgit. The Malaysian unit has fallen almost 12 percent against the dollar in the last month.
"Therefore, we will have to look at other measures that include deferring lumpy items," Anwar said.
Government officials have said previously they would look at ways of deferring projects and big-ticket import items.

Malaysia was expected to post a trade deficit this year of 1.65 billion ringgit against a deficit of 619 million last year. The deficit in the first six months of the year was 2.7 billion ringgit against a deficit of 687.8 million in the same period last year. ($1 = 2.76)
